decision_authority: owner-level (the R489 record typed the two options as owner/next-round work; the R490 operator directive named this decision as a round deliverable)
decision: OPTION (a) — the A2 adversarial gauntlet earns its own calibration; the calibration scope is NOT recorded as engine-instrument-scoped.
ruling_text: Article L binds every attacker whose results influence classification, not one instrument. The A2 gauntlet (a2/adversarial.py::adversarial_challenge — the conductor ATTACK stage's canonical implementation, adapters.py AttackEngineAdapter) influences classification terminally: its KILL is the run's final REJECTED (classify.py assembles the terminal reason). It has no calibration corpus, no sealed bars, and no shipped measurement. Until it earns its own calibration, its kills are recorded with the uncalibrated annotation, and the destination state is the R417 treatment at consumption: a KILL from an uncalibrated attacker is reclassified at consumption to ESCALATED_OBJECTION (objection + basis preserved verbatim; deterministic gates untouched).
why_option_a: Article L's plain text is general: 'Before attack results are allowed to influence world-class classification, a calibration corpus of known-defect + known-good mechanisms must exist... This makes the attacker a scientific instrument rather than a second LLM opinion.' Nothing in the article scopes it to the engine independent_attack instrument; the scoping would have to be authored by amendment.

Option (b) would exempt the exact attacker that terminally rejected the R489 cross-domain run (ts_f0880e025e60, 'obvious_combination: KILLED', served by the substituted free leg) — an exemption authored after the fact for the benefit of an unmeasured kill authority. That is the verifier-weakening direction (Art. VII's spirit; Art. XXXII's strongest-alternative-explanation test reads as self-serving), and it would grant authority that was never measured — the precise defect the R417 ruling removed from the engine instrument.

The R417 precedent already answered this shape of question for the engine instrument: measured non-selectivity (TPR 1.0 AND FPR 1.0, PPV == base rate) stripped the kill of terminal authority. The A2 gauntlet has no measurement at all — strictly less epistemic standing than the measured-not-calibrated engine instrument. Symmetric logic, stronger case.

The R488 live measurement additionally showed the attacker class is (rules x ring): the A2 gauntlet's transport selects from the same provider ring (adversarial.py llm_chat preferred_providers policy), so an uncalibrated A2 kill inherits the full ring-substitution exposure on top of the missing calibration.
